mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation (Taiwan Company Registration Certificate)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Taiwan Ministry of Economic Affairs, Department of Commercial Services
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Taiwan district court notary public notarization -> Taiwan Straits Exchange Foundation (SEF) certification -> Association for Relations Across the Taiwan Straits (ARATS) verification -> local PRC notary association confirmation -> filing with SAMR. No Hague Apostille is permitted and no PRC consular legalization step is chained because Taiwan is not an Apostille Convention party; this SEF/ARATS verification route is the exclusive consular-legalization-equivalent for cross-strait documents.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing (Current Company Status Certificate)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Taiwan Ministry of Economic Affairs, Department of Commercial Services
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Taiwan notary public notarization -> SEF certification -> ARATS verification -> local PRC notary association confirmation; do not add a Hague Apostille or PRC consulate legalization step. The verified copy is the only recognized form for PRC bank, tax, and SAMR use.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution and Power of Attorney authorizing the WFOE formation, capital contribution, and nominee for name clearance
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of Directors of the Taiwan investing company
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Board minutes and signature pages notarized by a Taiwan notary -> SEF certification -> ARATS verification -> submission to PRC notary association and MOFCOM/SAMR as required. This is a cross-strait consular-legalization-equivalent authentication, not a Hague Apostille, and cannot be chained with apostille or ordinary consular legalization.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Association (Amended and Consolidated) of the Taiwan investing company
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Taiwan investing company as approved by the Taiwan Ministry of Economic Affairs
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized certified true copy by Taiwan notary -> SEF certification -> ARATS verification; recognized subsequently for MOFCOM negative-list review, bank KYC, UBO filing, and commercial substance verification. No chained apostille or consular legalization is permitted.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter confirming the Taiwan investor's banking relationship and source of funds
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Taiwan commercial bank maintaining the investor's operating account
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Bank letterhead output with authorized signatory signature notarized in Taiwan -> SEF certification -> ARATS verification -> direct banker's confirmation to the PRC bank if requested under PBOC customer due diligence rules. Hague Apostille is not available for Taiwan documents; use the cross-strait consular-equivalent route only.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of every direct and indirect shareholder, UBO, director, supervisor, senior manager, commercial counterparty, ship master, vessel owner, and financing bank against the United Nations Security Council consolidated sanctions list; the PRC UN sanctions implementation and Ministry of Public Security terrorist/wanted lists; PBOC money-laundering risk and restrictive measures list; OFAC SDN List, 50 percent rule, CAATSA, and US maritime sanctions because USD wires and SWIFT may trigger US jurisdiction; EU and UK consolidated sanctions; FATF high-risk and monitored jurisdictions; and Taiwan's AML/anti-corruption registry and adverse media for cross-strait source-of-wealth verification. Enhanced due diligence is mandatory for politically exposed persons holding or controlling the Taiwan investor, PRC state-owned financial institution officials, high-risk jurisdictions, cash-intensive bunkering payments, and any flagged vessel calling at sanctioned ports including Iran, North Korea, Syria, Venezuela, or Crimea or exhibiting AIS/INS transparency anomalies. All screening results must be evidenced by timestamped search reports, match-analysis notes, and risk-rating memoranda before incorporation.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) National Enterprise Name Independent Declaration System, accessed through the local Municipal Market Supervision Administration's enterprise registration one-stop portal
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The registered name must be in simplified Chinese characters pursuant to the PRC Law on the Standard Spoken and Written Chinese Language; English letters, pinyin-only forms, and standalone Arabic numerals are not permitted in the legal name except in statutory exceptions for registered foreign-brand transliterations. The mandatory four-tier structure is [Administrative Division] + [Distinctive Trade Name] + [Industry or Operation Characteristics] + [Company Type, i.e., Limited Liability Company]. A Taiwanese investor with an English or romanized trade name must provide a phonetically transliterated Chinese distinctive element; the Chinese name is the only SAMR-registered legal name.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the name declaration is rejected by the SAMR system or manual review, the applicant receives a written rejection stating the legal basis. The applicant may first request a manual re-review through the enterprise name declaration portal within 15 business days. If the manual re-review is denied, the applicant may file an administrative reconsideration application with the next-higher market supervision administration or with the same-level people's government within 60 days from receipt of the denial under the PRC Administrative Reconsideration Law. If the reconsideration decision is adverse or not timely rendered, the applicant may institute an administrative lawsuit in the competent People's Court within 6 months. Filing a new name declaration with a materially different distinctive element is the fastest practical remedy and does not waive the pending appeal rights.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office, commercial mailbox, or agent-only address is not permissible for a PRC WFOE engaged in marine fuel bunkering. SAMR requires a substantive physical registered address in the registration locality; the State Taxation Administration requires an actual place of business for invoice control, tax registration, and on-site inspections; and commercial banks will reject a virtual office for corporate account opening because PBOC customer due diligence rules demand physical verification of business premises. For the bunkering industry, the registered office must also house contracts, voyage records, accounting books, and management substance. A serviced office with a genuine lease, on-site staff, and record access may be accepted, but a virtual office product per se is not.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Likelihood: High - approximately 70 percent estimated probability of unannounced inspection within the first 12 months following issue of the maritime fuel supply license and VAT/customs registration. Checklist of inspection triggers: (1) business scope includes ship fueling, bunkering, and lubricant supply; (2) application for duty-free bunker fuel quotas or export VAT exemption; (3) port authority registration; (4) cross-border payments under standby letters of credit; (5) PBOC/SAMR UBO annual updates; (6) tax risk profiling of the shipping and fuel industry. Inspectors will verify physical premises, original lease, payroll, accounting system, bank statements, and board records. Failure can result in revocation of license, bank account freezing, and deregistration.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Taiwan Company Act, as codified under the Ministry of Economic Affairs, particularly Articles 1-5, 12, 15, 128-131, 148-156 on company formation and capital, Articles 172, 192, 202, 208 and 228 on board powers and director appointment, and Articles 370-386 on recognition and registration of foreign-invested companies; together with the Statute for Investment by Foreign Nationals and the Company Registration Rules established by the MOEA Department of Commercial Services.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Department of Commercial Services, Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA), Taiwan (R.O.C.), acting through the National Company Registration One-Stop Online Portal at gcis.nat.gov.tw.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Company Formation Registration Application with notarized Articles of Incorporation, the pro forma First Board Resolution, and the supporting foreign investment approval letter.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital applies to a Taiwan limited company under the Company Act. However, the Investment Commission of MOEA, when approving a 100% foreign-owned company, will assess capital adequacy and requires the subscribed capital to be remitted and deposited in a blocked Taiwan bank escrow account designated for the company before registration. The escrow funds can be released only after the Company Registration Certificate is issued and the capital verification report by a Taiwan certified public accountant is filed with the registry.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLUTION OF THE FIRST MEETING OF THE BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF [CN_WFOE_LTD], A COMPANY LIMITED BY SHARES INCORPORATED IN TAIWAN (R.O.C.). THIS PRO FORMA RESOLUTION IS ADOPTED BY THE SOLE INCORPORATING SHAREHOLDER AND THE INITIAL DIRECTORS IN ACCORDANCE WITH THE TAIWAN COMPANY ACT AND THE ARTICLES OF INCORPORATION. WHEREAS the sole shareholder has resolved to incorporate the Company as a wholly foreign-owned enterprise for the purpose of carrying on offshore marine fuel bunkering, lubricant replenishment and ancillary port logistics services; and WHEREAS the Company has received the approval of the Investment Commission of the Ministry of Economic Affairs and has satisfied all foreign investment conditions; NOW, THEREFORE, the Board unanimously resolves as follows: 1. Capital subscription. The Board confirms that the authorized share capital of the Company is New Taiwan Dollars [ ] divided into [ ] ordinary shares with par value of New Taiwan Dollars 10 each. The sole shareholder has subscribed in full the initially issued and paid-up capital of New Taiwan Dollars [ ], which has been credited to the blocked capital account No. [ ] at [ ] Bank. The directors certify that the cash subscriptions have been paid, no shares have been issued at a discount, no bearer shares have been issued, and the paid-in capital is fully available for the corporate objects of offshore marine fuel bunkering, lubricant replenishment and ancillary port services. 2. Registered office. The Board adopts the place located at [ ] as the registered office, principal place of business, and address for service of process and all statutory notices. The Chairman is directed to lease the premises, post the corporate name plate, and notify the Department of Commercial Services, Ministry of Economic Affairs, of any future change of registered office. 3. Banking authorization. The Board authorizes and instructs the opening of demand, foreign currency, and standby letter of credit accounts at [ ] Bank and at the port-related bank [ ]. The General Manager, together with the Chief Financial Officer or the Company Secretary, are designated joint authorized signatories for all payment instructions, SWIFT wires, LC applications, import and export settlements, receivables, and treasury transactions. A specimen of the company seal, the chop of the Chairman, and this resolution shall be lodged with each bank. 4. Statutory officers. The Board appoints [ ] as Chairperson and Managing Director, [ ] as General Manager, [ ] as Chief Financial Officer, and [ ] as Company Secretary and Chief Compliance Officer. The officers are authorized to execute and file all documents required by the Taiwan Company Act, tax, customs, labor, environmental, port authorities, and the Maritime Port Bureau. The Company Secretary shall organize statutory books, minutes, share register, and filings. 5. General authorization. All directors and officers are authorized to instruct notaries public, certified public accountants, lawyers, tax agents, port surveyors, and the Company Registration One-Stop Online Portal service provider to complete registration, obtain the unified business tax identity number, stamps, permits and certificates, and to incur ordinary and necessary expenses for this incorporation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Foreign Investment Approval and Name Reservation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Investment Commission, Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA), Taiwan; online via Invest in Taiwan portal and the MOEA Company Name Reservation service.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the investment application to the Investment Commission before any company formation filing. The application must state the foreign investor, ultimate beneficial owners, the capital amount, the proposed Taiwan registered office, directors, and the ISIC 5222 marine bunkering business plan. Attach audited financial statements or bank reference of the parent. The Investment Commission will screen the investment for restricted or negative-list activities, national security concerns, and compliance with Taiwan foreign investment rules. Upon approval, obtain the investment approval letter. Concurrently use the MOEA Company Name Reservation service to ensure the proposed English and Mandarin corporate names are not identical or deceptively similar to an existing registered Taiwanese company. The name reservation is valid for six months. In parallel, contact the Maritime Port Bureau for a preliminary non-objection letter confirming the availability of port premises, wharf access, and bunkering operation eligibility at the intended harbor.
required_dossiers: International investment application form completed in English and Chinese
Certificate of incorporation and board resolution of the 100% foreign parent shareholder, legalized or apostilled and translated by a Taiwan notary public
Passport or national ID copies of all directors and the ultimate beneficial owner
Bank reference letter and source-of-funds statement
Business plan for offshore marine fuel bunkering and lubricant replenishment under ISIC 5222
Letter of intent or lease for port office and storage site
Preliminary no-objection letter from Maritime Port Bureau if secured before filing
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Investment Commission issues a query, file a written explanation and supplementary evidence through the Invest in Taiwan case page within 14 days. If the name reservation is rejected due to identical or confusing similarity, submit up to three alternate names. If the investment is suspended on national security or restricted-industry grounds, restructure the shareholding or reduce the foreign ownership percentage and apply for pre-screening; an administrative appeal to the Executive Yuan is available.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarization of Articles of Incorporation and Adoption of First Board Resolution
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Taiwan Notary Public appointed by the district court of the registered office; for home-jurisdiction documents, the Taiwan Economic and Cultural Office or competent apostille authority.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Following the investment approval, execute the bilingual Articles of Incorporation and the First Board Resolution. The notary must verify the identity and legal capacity of the shareholder representatives, directors and officer appointees. All foreign corporate documents must be notarized in the home jurisdiction, authenticated by apostille or Taiwan Economic and Cultural Office legalization, translated into Mandarin by a certified translator, and then presented to the Taiwan notary. The Articles must set out the corporate name, registered office, principal objects including bunkering, physical supply of marine fuel and lubricants, storage, and ancillary logistics, share classes, authorized and paid-in capital, director and supervisor provisions, and indemnity arrangements. The First Board Resolution must approve share subscriptions, adopt the registered office, authorize bank account opening, and appoint statutory officers. After notarization, the signature books and corporate seal are executed. This step is mandatory before the MOEA registration filing.
required_dossiers: Approved foreign investment letter from MOEA Investment Commission
Notarized incorporation certificate and board authorization of the sole foreign shareholder with apostille or Taiwan Economic and Cultural Office legalization
Certified Mandarin translation of the parent shareholder resolution
Draft Articles of Incorporation in Chinese and English
Pro forma First Board Resolution signed by all initial directors
Identity documentation for all directors, supervisors, and officers
Proof of registered office address in the form of a draft lease or letter of intent
Notary engagement letter and fee receipt
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary identifies an inconsistency between the English and Chinese versions, revise the bilingual text and re-execute before all parties. If legalization or apostille is incomplete, arrange re-legalization through the Taiwan Economic and Cultural Office or the issuing foreign authority. If the foreign shareholder board resolution lacks express authority for the Taiwan business, obtain a supplemental parent board resolution and re-notarize.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Department of Commercial Services, Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA), National Company Registration One-Stop Online Portal at gcis.nat.gov.tw.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The appointed attorney or certified public accountant submits the Company Formation Registration Application online together with the notarized Articles of Incorporation, First Board Resolution, the Investment Commission approval letter, capital remittance certificate from the Taiwan foreign exchange bank, and the CPA capital verification report. The online system will calculate the filing fee; pay such fee by online transfer or at the designated counter bank. The MOEA examiner verifies company name uniqueness, lawful business scope, the registered office address in Taiwan, minimum directors and quorum, and the absence of strike-off or disqualification of directors. Once approved, MOEA issues the Company Registration Certificate and the unified business number, which is the tax identification number. The company becomes a valid Taiwan legal person on the date of registration. After receiving the certificate, the WFOE must apply for business registration, uniform invoice registration, and tax entity registration with the National Taxation Administration. This step concludes statutory incorporation.
required_dossiers: Company Formation Registration Application submitted online
Notarized Articles of Incorporation
Notarized First Board Resolution
Foreign investment approval letter from MOEA Investment Commission
Capital remittance and foreign exchange certificate from the receiving Taiwanese bank
CPA capital verification report
Registered office lease or ownership certificate and landlord consent
Identification and specimen signatures of directors and officers
Company registration filing fee payment receipt
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the MOEA portal rejects due to formal deficiencies, refile corrected documents within the objection period, generally 15 days, without losing the original order number. If an error arises in business scope under ISIC 5222, amend the Articles and resubmit shareholder resolution. If the name is conflicting, use the reserved alternative name. A formal rejection can be appealed under the Administrative Procedure Act within 30 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax, Customs, Labour and Bank Account Activation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Taxation Administration of the Ministry of Finance, Taiwan Customs Administration, Bureau of Labor Insurance, and the authorized foreign exchange bank designated in the Investment Commission letter.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Immediately after MOEA registration, the WFOE must open fully operational bank accounts and obtain a uniform invoice number by registering for Taiwan profit-seeking enterprise income tax, business tax, value-added tax, and withholding tax. The original escrow or blocked capital account is released to the operational account upon presentation of the Company Registration Certificate and the CPA verification report. The entity must register as a taxpayer with the local National Taxation Administration branch, apply for customs registration if it will import fuel additives, lubricants or equipment, register as an employer with the Bureau of Labor Insurance for labor and health insurance, and post the required occupational safety notice. The WFOE should also notify the Maritime Port Bureau of its commercial launch schedule and submit updated tax and insurance certificates to obtain the port access card. All filings should be completed within 30 days after registration to avoid late fees.
required_dossiers: Company Registration Certificate from MOEA
Company seal and responsible person seal specimen
Unified business number registration application
National Taxation Administration taxpayer registration form
Customs registration application if importing marine fuel, additives, or equipment
Bureau of Labor Insurance employer registration form
Bank account opening package and authorized signatory resolution
Registered office lease and company incorporation documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the taxation administration queries the application, submit supplementary statements and the relevant MOEA certificate. If a late registration penalty is assessed, request abatement by showing reasonable cause. If the bank requires further anti-money laundering and know-your-customer information, provide the ultimate beneficial ownership declaration and source-of-funds documents. If the escrow release is delayed, obtain a follow-up confirmation from the Investment Commission and the central bank reporting code.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Industrial Operating License and Bunkering Facility Approval
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Maritime Port Bureau of the Ministry of Transportation and Communications, local city or county Fire Bureau, Ministry of Environment of Taiwan, and the port harbor company occupational safety office.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Before beginning physical bunkering or lubricant replenishment, submit a formal application to the Maritime Port Bureau for a port service and bunkering supplier license. The application must include the port facility security plan, environmental emergency response plan, bunker fuel transfer procedures, spill containment plan, insurance certificates, hazardous material storage and transfer manifest, and evidence of fire certificate. The Port Bureau will inspect the proposed quay or storage location, verify barge or fixed pipeline integrity, calibration of fuel meters, anti-overfill devices, vapor emission controls, and the adequacy of the facility health and safety management system. After inspection and payment of the port service fee, the Bureau issues a bunkering operating permit with annual throughput conditions. Concurrently, submit the civil defense fire safety permit application, an environmental impact assessment registration or environmental review submission to the Ministry of Environment, and the workplace clearance application to the occupational safety and health inspection office. No fuel may be sold or delivered until all permits are issued and posted at the port facility.
required_dossiers: Bunkering supplier license application form of the Maritime Port Bureau
Company registration certificate and tax identification certificate
Port facility lease, concession, or letter of no objection
Bunker fuel quality and quantity assurance manual
Spill prevention, control, and countermeasure plan
Fire safety plan and civil defense fire permit application
Environmental impact assessment registration or full EIA report, as classified
Barge, vessel, or facility insurance certificate
Calibration certificates for fuel flow meters and tank gauges
Occupational safety and health management plan and audit records
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the port authority issues an inspection finding, the WFOE must fix nonconformities and submit a corrective action report within 30 days. If the civil defense fire permit is refused, install required firefighting systems, vapor detection, portable extinguishers and emergency alarms, then request re-inspection. If the Ministry of Environment rejects an environmental registration or requires a full EIA, commission an environmental consultant, submit an impact assessment, and implement all mitigation measures; the operating license remains suspended until final environmental clearance.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Maritime Port Bureau, Ministry of Transportation and Communications, Taiwan; together with the local port harbor company and the city or county Fire Bureau.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Port Service Provider and Bunkering Fuel Supply License, issued under the Maritime Port Bureau Port Rules and the Commercial Port Act.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry of Environment, Executive Yuan, Taiwan, formerly the Environmental Protection Administration.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category C environmental registration for small harbor bunkering and service areas; Category B environmental review and EIA mitigation plan for fuel storage tanks above 5,000 metric tonnes or annual bunker transfer above 50,000 cubic metres; a full Category A EIA report is required if the facility is within 1 kilometre of sensitive coastal, fishery, conservation or residential zones or handles fuel with high sulphur or VOC content.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Quantitative compliance: wastewater discharge pH 6.0 to 9.0, biochemical oxygen demand BOD5 not exceeding 30 mg/L, chemical oxygen demand COD not exceeding 100 mg/L, total suspended solids not exceeding 30 mg/L, oil and grease not exceeding 10 mg/L, ammonia nitrogen not exceeding 10 mg/L, and no visible oily sheen; stormwater from tank areas must be segregated and permitted. Volatile organic compound vapor emissions at loading arms and barge connections must be controlled to a 95 percent recovery or abatement efficiency using vapor balancing or emission control equipment, with stack VOC concentration not exceeding 50 parts per million as methane equivalent. Hazardous waste including slops, oily rags, spent filters and contaminated soil must be stored in closed containers for no more than 180 days, manifested and delivered to a licensed hazardous waste treatment facility; used oil is regulated under the Waste Disposal Act. Marine fuel products must meet Taiwan CNS marine fuel standards and the applicable sulphur limit for sulphur oxide emission control areas.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Before operation, the facility must obtain a Fire Safety Certificate and Civil Defense Dangerous Goods Storage Permit from the local Fire Bureau; pass structural load and seismic inspections of tanks, bunker piers and pipe supports conducted by a Taiwan laboratory accredited engineering firm; and secure the Occupational Safety and Health Inspection Office clearance under the Occupational Safety and Health Act, covering evacuation drills, fire alarm and gas detection, personal protective equipment, hot-work permits, confined-space entry procedures, storage tank gas-freeing, and a statutory emergency response plan approved by the port fire brigade.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Ministry of Finance (Taiwan), Taxation Administration, through the regional National Taxation Bureaus; online electronic tax portal: the Ministry of Finance e-Tax Portal (https://www.etax.nat.gov.tw).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: The CN_WFOE_LTD foreign-invested limited liability company is first incorporated under the Taiwan Company Act. The foreign investor applies for investment approval under the Statute for Investment by Foreign Nationals with the Investment Commission, Ministry of Economic Affairs, unless an exemption applies. Company registration with the Ministry of Economic Affairs Central Registration Office triggers the issuance of the statutory eight-digit Unified Business Number (UBN), which is the tax identification number (TIN) used for all Taiwan tax filings. Before commencing business, the WFOE must complete tax registration with the local National Taxation Bureau, register as a value-added business tax taxpayer, register its uniform-invoice scheme, and register as a withholding agent for employee and non-resident payments. If a foreign non-resident entity establishes a Taiwan branch instead of a subsidiary, the head office must appoint a statutory tax representative and the branch must obtain a separate UBN; a foreign non-resident without a fixed place of business performing Taiwan-source activities is obliged to register or appoint a withholding agent under the Income Tax Act.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None (Taiwan does not have a check-the-box election or a hybrid-mismatch check-the-box regime. A foreign investor can select at formation whether to operate as a Taiwan subsidiary or as a branch of the foreign head office, and that choice determines taxable-entity status; otherwise classification is governed by the Company Act and the Income Tax Act.)

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (Taiwan Business Tax under the Value-added and Non-value-added Business Tax Act)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: NTD 80,000 average monthly taxable sales for goods and NTD 40,000 for services; mandatory VAT registration is required above these thresholds, and businesses with average monthly sales exceeding NTD 200,000 must additionally adopt the uniform-invoice issuance system.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Taiwan mandates Uniform Invoices for registered business tax suppliers. Under the Ministry of Finance e-Invoice scheme, qualifying suppliers must transmit e-invoice data to the Ministry of Finance e-Invoice platform through the government Turnkey API service; each e-invoice is assigned a unique invoice number and random anti-fraud code by the platform. The platform performs automated cross-validation between invoice issuance, VAT monthly return filing, and payment records; there is no physical fiscal stamping requirement, but API-based transmission, retention, and periodic declaration are mandatory for participating e-invoice issuers.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: A registered Taiwan VAT business may claim 0% zero rating for exported goods, services directly related to exports, and goods or services supplied to international transportation. For marine bunkering and lubricant replenishment, zero rating is available where the fuel or lubricant is delivered under Customs supervision to an outbound ocean-going vessel engaged in international trade, the vessel departs Taiwan for a foreign port, the supply is evidenced by a Customs export declaration and bunker delivery documentation, and the purchase consideration is received in foreign exchange from a non-Taiwan buyer or the vessel operator. Qualifying offshore digital services supplied to foreign enterprises are capable of zero rating when they are exported, used outside Taiwan, and supported by foreign-currency remittance evidence.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Bill of Entry) confirming bunker fuel/lubricant quantity and date of export release
Bill of Lading, sea waybill, or port/Customs departure clearance proving the vessel's outbound international voyage
Inward Remittance Certificate (FIRC) issued by an authorized Taiwan bank evidencing receipt of foreign-currency payment from the non-resident shipowner, charterer, or buyer
Bunker delivery note or fuel supply report with IMO vessel identification, grade, quantity, and supplier details
Zero-rated Uniform Invoice issued and declared in accordance with the Value-added and Non-value-added Business Tax Act
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The National Taxation Bureau will audit the end-to-end link among the Customs export declaration, bill of lading/voyage evidence, bunker delivery note, zero-rated invoice, and the inward foreign exchange record. Missing or inconsistent export substantiation causes the zero rate to be reversed and the tax authority will assess the underpaid VAT at 5%, add overdue interest, impose a surcharge of up to five times the tax evaded under the Business Tax Act, and may claw back any refunded or claimed input VAT. False or manipulated export documentation can additionally attract Customs penalties and criminal tax-evasion prosecution under the Tax Collection Act, with retrospective reassessment extending to the statutory review period.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: The People's Bank of China (PBOC) and the State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE) for the onshore CN WFOE; the Taiwan-based investing entity is also subject to the central monetary authority of the Taiwan jurisdiction (commonly cited as the CBC) under the Foreign Exchange Regulation Act for outward remittances.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: China operates a strictly managed floating exchange-rate regime. The current account has been liberalized to permit RMB convertibility for bona fide trade and service transactions; a WFOE may freely convert and remit current-account proceeds for imported bunker fuel, port fees, crew costs and marine lubricant replenishment once supporting trade documents and tax certificates are filed with the handling bank. The capital account, however, remains closed: equity capital injections, debt issuance, cross-border loans and repatriation of registered capital require separate SAFE registration, a qualified local custodian structure and often post-payment verification. Profit remittances are permitted only after statutory annual audit and with proof of paid corporate income tax; the distribution itself must be routed through the SAFE-registered capital account or RMB settlement account, and the bank will check the audited financial statements, board resolution, and shareholder approval. In practice, the WFOE must keep an audited Chinese currency balance sheet, file the SAFE annual FDI report, and obtain a capital account payment confirmation before wiring dividends to Taiwan. Certainty of settlement is lower for TWD than USD or RMB, but RMB/USD current-account payments are generally executable at the commercial bank counter.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under SAFE Goods Trade Foreign Exchange Administration, export proceeds from marine fuel sales to international vessels must be repatriated to a domestic foreign exchange current-account account within 180 days of the customs export declaration date. The mandatory conversion ratio is zero: no stipulated percentage must be sold to the banking system; the enterprise may retain the proceeds in foreign exchange or convert them to RMB at its own election. All receipts must be reported in the SAFE Total Amount Verification system, and the receiving bank must cross-check the declared export value, commodity code, vessel identification data and bunkering evidence against the sales contract.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Bank of China Limited (BOC), Shanghai Branch
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: FDI registered foreign exchange capital account and RMB basic deposit settlement account

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Industrial and Commercial Bank of China Limited (ICBC)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: RMB operational settlement account, trade financing line, and cross-border expense settlement account
Standby letter of credit collateral account, foreign exchange settlement account, and operating liquidity account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Offshore fintech EMIs are not legally viable for the onshore WFOE. PBOC Payment Management Regulations require any entity providing payment or clearing services to a Chinese legal entity to hold a PRC payment institution license; a foreign EMI cannot open a basic deposit account or foreign exchange account for the WFOE, cannot hold segregated client funds for the WFOE, and cannot register as the executing bank for SAFE capital or current-account records. An overseas EMI may only invoice the Taiwan parent offshore, but if used to route WFOE receipts or capital it will fail SAFE receipt and declaration bank-of-record compliance and trigger frozen funds, penalties and possible licence revocation. Viability rating: Low.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: A physical in-branch appearance is mandatory for at least the legal representative of the WFOE, being the executive director, chairman or general manager designated in the articles of association, when opening the RMB basic deposit account. Remote consular or proxy-only account opening is not accepted by PBOC-governed commercial banks. The Taiwan shareholder must deliver a notarized certificate of incorporation, updated registry excerpt, and a board resolution appointing the China legal representative and authorizing bank signatories; the Taiwan documents must be notarized domestically and verified through the cross-strait document verification channel. Original passports, PRC work or residence certificates where applicable, company chops, and lease or ownership documents for the registered office are required on the day of the interview.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Ultimate beneficial owner (UBO) chain terminates in a Taiwan holding structure with nominees and no visible operational substance for the bunkering business.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarized Taiwan incorporation documents and articles of association; up-to-date Ministry of Economic Affairs company extract showing all directors and beneficial owners; complete shareholder register for every intermediate entity up to natural persons; passport copies of the UBOs; source-of-wealth file comprising Taiwan tax returns, bank statements, share-purchase contracts and notarized affidavits from transferors; signed organizational chart with percentage holdings.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Marine bunkering inherently creates sanctions, flag-state and vessel-identity risk because fuel could be supplied to designated vessels or used for illicit ship-to-ship transfers.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: IMO ship identification number and flag registry certificate for each bunkered vessel; owner, operator, charterer and manager line-up; OFAC, EU, UN and China sanctions screening results; International Ship Security Certificate and port state control inspection history; commercial charter party or voyage orders; bunker delivery note incorporating supplied fuel grade, quantity, vessel IMO and port call; independent surveyor flowmeter and quantity report.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Trade-based money-laundering red flag arises from mismatches among the customs export declaration, the physical fuel quantity evidenced by flowmeters and bunker delivery notes, and the SAFE export receipt verification window.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: SAFE total-amount verification report; customs export declaration form with correct marine fuel and bunker HS classification; commercial invoice and packing list; signed bunker delivery note; independent weight or surveyor report; bill of lading or port-authority service statement; bank MT103 or MT202 routing evidence; benchmark price reconciliation against Platts and MOPAG and the underlying international marine fuel sales contract.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: The WFOE has no valid onshore operating licence or the registered address, lease and tax filings do not match the claimed ISIC 5222 bunkering operation.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Current PRC business licence with the approved scope covering marine fuel bunkering and lubricant replenishment; valid port or fuel-operation business licence from the competent transport and port authority; hazardous chemical, petroleum storage and operation permits; tax registration certificates and recent VAT and income tax filings; registered-office lease agreement with rental receipts and utility bills; audited financial statements and CPA opening capital verification report; proof of staff labour contracts and social-insurance enrolment.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: The Taiwan parent must first obtain CBC outward remittance approval or blanket approval, if applicable, and remit through a Taiwan clearing bank by SWIFT MT103. The Chinese WFOE must complete FDI registration with SAFE through the receiving bank and obtain the FDI business registration confirmation before inbound settlement. The MT103 must show the purpose narrative as equity injection to the WFOE, with the SAFE FDI registration number and the correct BOP transaction code from the SAFE Cross-Border Receipts and Payments Classification; the handling bank will map the exact code at account creation. The inward USD or RMB is credited to the WFOE FDI capital account and can be settled only under the payment-after-verification regime after documentation is uploaded to the SAFE or bank system. Capital verification is evidenced by a PRC certified public accountant capital verification report addressed to the company, confirming paid-in registered capital from the Taiwan remittance against the approved registered capital amount.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: The primary clearing rail for operating and inventory payments is SWIFT MT103 for direct wire disbursements to qualified suppliers, port agents, barge operators and tax authorities, supported by the underlying sales or purchase contracts, invoices, tax certificates and customs or port declarations. For high-value fuel procurement and marine lubricant replenishment, the WFOE should use a commercial letter of credit under MT700 or MT707, with a standby letter of credit under MT760 to secure performance guarantees or vessel supply contracts. Documentary collections under D/P and D/A terms may be used for established counterparties. RMB cross-strait payments should, where available, be cleared through CIPS rather than a plain SWIFT or CHIPS path; USD disbursements should clear through the US correspondent network via the receiving bank. Every outbound current-account payment must quote the relevant SAFE purpose code and retain supporting vouchers for at least six to ten years.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore deliverable RMB foreign-exchange forward contracts with the handling bank, supported by real trade contracts and SAFE trade-background documentation.
Foreign-exchange swaps between RMB and USD for matching short-term liquidity mismatches in bunker procurement, subject to the same real-transaction rule.

Cross-currency interest-rate swaps and foreign-exchange swaps for long-term external financing or registered capital optimization, permitted only after SAFE external-debt registration where the WFOE is a borrower or guarantor.

Offshore non-deliverable forwards are not permissible for the onshore WFOE because they lack the required Chinese underlying settlement purpose; the Taiwan parent may independently layer an offshore NDF outside China, but the WFOE cannot be a contract party.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Profit-Seeking Enterprise Income Tax Settlement Return (annual corporate income tax return)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Tax Administration, Ministry of Finance, Taiwan (National Taxation Administration; jurisdiction registered office branch)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: 1 May to 31 May following the calendar tax year; electronic filing and CPA-attested filing may extend to 30 June; if the statutory date falls on a holiday, the next business day applies
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing without approved extension triggers late-filing surcharge of 1% of the tax due for every two days late, up to 10%; continued non-compliance after Tax Administration demand permits official assessment plus under-reporting penalty up to 100% of the short-paid tax; unpaid tax bears daily interest and may be referred to compulsory collection after a 30-day demand

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Business Tax and Uniform Invoice Bimonthly Return (value-added tax filing series)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Tax Administration, Ministry of Finance, Taiwan (regional VAT service office)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 15 days after the close of every two-month VAT period: Jan-Feb by 15 Mar; Mar-Apr by 15 May; May-Jun by 15 Jul; Jul-Aug by 15 Sep; Sep-Oct by 15 Nov; Nov-Dec by 15 Jan of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file by the statutory date exposes the company to administrative penalty of NT$3,600 per return and an additional delinquency tax of 1% for every two days, up to 15%; where the late return carries unreported output VAT, the short-paid tax is collected with interest and a penalty not exceeding 100% of the assessed amount

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Withholding Tax and Earnings/Income Statement Reconciliation Return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Tax Administration, Ministry of Finance, Taiwan (withholding registration office)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Submit all prior-year withholding, interest, royalty, and salary earnings statements by 31 January of the following year for domestic recipients; non-residents are withheld at source on each payment date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing of the annual withholding statement subjects the responsible person to fines under the Tax Collection Act and Income Tax Act, typically commencing at NT$1,500 per statement and rising with the amount of undistributed withholding tax; under-withholding is collected from the company with interest and may trigger an evasion penalty up to 100% of the underpaid amount

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Ordinary Shareholders Meeting, Financial Statements Approval and Surplus Appropriation Resolution (with statutory register update)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs, Department of Commerce; registers maintained at the registered office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after fiscal year end, i.e. no later than 30 June; if a special review or consolidated group scheduling applies, the annual general meeting may be postponed only by resolution and with applicable regulatory notice
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: If the Ministry of Economic Affairs or a shareholder requests a meeting and the directors fail to convene, the court or competent authority may convoke it; responsible directors are subject to fines under the Company Act for refusal to comply, and civil liability for dividends or distributions if financial statements are not timely approved. Government registration fees apply only if an amendment is registered contemporaneously

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Company Beneficial Ownership / UBO Register Annual Confirmation and Amendment Filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Company Registration Office, Ministry of Economic Affairs, Taiwan
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 days after any change in controlling shareholder, ultimate beneficial owner, director, supervisor, or senior manager; as a calendar checkpoint, reconfirm by the annual shareholders meeting date but no later than 30 June and document the confirmation in the minute book
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file or update the UBO declaration is a regulatory offence carrying administrative fines under the Money Laundering Control Act and Company Act; responsible officers may be fined per violation and the company's commercial registration may be marked non-compliant in AML risk assessments. Persistent non-compliance may lead to restriction of filing rights and administrative enforcement after due procedure

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Bunkering License and Port Operating Concession Annual Renewal / Endorsement
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Bureau of Energy, Ministry of Economic Affairs; Maritime Port Bureau / Taiwan International Ports Corporation, Ltd. for port area site license
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually no fewer than 30 days before the license anniversary date; for calendar-year port permits, renewal application must be submitted by 30 November to be approved before 31 December
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Operating without renewed license triggers suspension of bunker supply operations, removal from port fuel supplier list, and administrative fines imposed under the Petroleum Act and Port Act; intentional unlicensed operations can reach NT$5,000,000 and revocation of the WFOE's business registration

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: An independent certified public accountant audit is legally mandatory under Taiwan Commercial Accounting Act and FSC/MOF regulations when, at the balance sheet date or during the fiscal year, the WFOE meets any of: (i) paid-in capital of NT$30,000,000 or more; (ii) annual operating revenue of NT$50,000,000 or more; (iii) total assets exceeding NT$100,000,000; (iv) the entity is a public company, financial institution, or an enterprise designated by the competent authority because of industry, monopoly, or public interest; (v) the enterprise files consolidated financial statements or is the subsidiary of a public or internationally listed group required to be audited for group reporting; (vi) headcount exceeds 100 regular employees and the enterprise is not eligible for the simplified SME accounting concession; or (vii) the Energy Bureau, Port Authority, bank, or insurance counterparty requires an audited balance sheet as a condition of the bunkering license, port concession, bonded fuel storage, or credit facility. Threshold figures are periodically adjusted by the Ministry of Finance; a company that exceeded any threshold in the prior fiscal year must retain a CPA in the current year.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Applicable standards are Taiwan IFRSs (TFRS) for public and large non-public companies, and for private WFOEs below the audit thresholds the Taiwan IFRS for SMEs or ROC Business Entity Accounting Standards (ROC GAAP) electively, provided the choice is consistently applied and complies with the Commercial Accounting Act. Specific measurement rules for bunker inventories follow IAS 2, revenue from bunker supply and service contracts follows IFRS 15, and any time or tanker charters, storage leases, or port terminal licensing is measured under IFRS 16. The annual statutory financial statements must be presented in New Taiwan Dollars and, for consolidation into the PRC parent, a reconciliation note to PRC GAAP or IFRS is required.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Taiwan's Company Act and Money Laundering Control Act require a non-public company to keep a current UBO/controlling shareholder register and register the information with the Ministry of Economic Affairs within 30 days of incorporation and within 30 days after any shareholding transfer or change in beneficial ownership, directors, supervisors, or senior managers. There is no separate annual UBO return form for every dormant WFOE, but the board must reconfirm the register at the annual shareholders meeting, ratify no-change or file a 30-day amendment if a transfer occurred, and preserve shareholders' written transfer instruments together with the register of members. The company's statutory annual confirmation window is therefore the signing date of the financial statements or the AGM resolution, in practice no later than 30 June; a transfer registered during the year is reported using the normal 30-day UBO amendment window.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (Shareholders) and share transfer records
Register of Charges/Mortgages and pledges over company assets
Minute Book of shareholders and board of directors meetings
Register of corporate seals and share certificate stubs
UBO/controlling shareholder register and supporting declarations

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: 800-2,500 per year for registered office, corporate secretarial agent, annual filing support and local legal publications; a Taipei commercial agent with banking/AML compliance files typically falls in the upper half of this range
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: 4,000-9,000 for a first-time or continuing CPA audit of a bunkering WFOE with moderate volume and a clean structure; IFRS conversion notes, group audit arrangements, or port authority-specific audit schedules may add 20-30%

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 20% single headline rate for profit-seeking enterprises, effective for fiscal years beginning on or after 1 January 2018
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No municipal or provincial corporate income tax surcharge exists above the national 20% tax. Tax incentives available to a licensed bunkering operator include: research and development investment credits of up to 15% of qualifying R&D expenditure (applicable where a Taiwan entity maintains fuel-blending or marine-lubricant R&D activity), investment tax credits of up to 5% for qualifying smart-equipment and green-energy purchases used in storage and barge operations, and the 5% retained earnings surtax on undistributed profits is the only additional entity-level tax. Temporary reduction is not available for maritime fuel trading; the 20% rate is a final entity-level burden.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Profit-Seeking Enterprise Income Tax Annual Return (General Closing Return) together with the Balance Sheet, Income Statement, Retained Earnings Surcharge Return, and related schedules; mandatory electronic filing through the Ministry of Finance E-Tax Portal (tax.nat.gov.tw) using the MOEA Business Certificate (commerce credential) or tax practitioner digital certificate.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual closing return (fiscal-year basis); provisional tax filing for the first six months is due 1-30 September each year based on 50% of the prior year's tax; monthly withholding statements (as applicable) are aggregated and filed by 31 January of the following year.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The annual return must be filed within five months after the end of the fiscal year; for a calendar-year entity, the statutory deadline is 31 May. A one-month general extension to 30 June is commonly announced by the Ministry of Finance, and a taxpayer-specific extension may be granted upon application where books and records are under audit or for force majeure.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Company legal name, Uniform Serial Number (Tax ID), registered address, principal business activity code per the Taiwan Industry Standard Classification, and the ISIC-derived activity description for marine fuel bunkering and lubricant replenishment.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The Taiwan operating entity must reconcile its business registration, fuel-supply licence issued by the Bureau of Energy, and the tax return's principal business code; non-resident shareholders should ensure the filed address and responsible person records correspond to the effective management and control location in Taiwan.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross revenue and net sales revenue from bunker fuel supply, marine lubricant sales, and barging/replenishment services, net of sales discounts, returns, and trade allowances.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report all revenue from deliveries made in Taiwan's territorial waters, port anchorage zones, and bonded storage premises; maintain IMO numbers of vessels supplied, bills of lading, available supply dockets, and SWIFT/LC payment records to evidence the commercial substance of each non-resident-facing sale.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Cost of marine fuel purchased from refiners, suppliers, or related trading companies; inbound freight and insurance; terminal fees; and customs duty/excise (petroleum product tax) paid at importation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Transfer-pricing adjustments must be reflected where the parent is a Chinese or Hong Kong procurement entity; arm's-length cost benchmarks from Singapore or Fujian refuelling supply points must be documented in the TP file before cost deductions are allowed.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductible operating expenses including storage facility rents, barge maintenance and charter hire, mooring and berth charges, salaries of bunker traders and marine operations staff, insurance, professional fees, and administrative overhead.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Any management fee, technical service charge, or IP royalty paid to the non-resident parent must satisfy the benefit test and be supported by contemporaneous TP documentation; deductible expenses require valid VAT invoices or authorised paid-foreign-payment vouchers with withholding tax evidence.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 29 Taxable Income / Loss Carryforward Schedule
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Annual taxable income before applying prior-year loss deductions; the schedule identifies the ten-year loss carryforward entitlement and current-year set-off amount.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Loss carryforward is allowed only where the enterprise keeps proper accounting books and has filed audited returns for loss years; a non-resident-owned bunkering entity should preserve tax bureau receipts and assessment records for each loss year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Calculation of profit-seeking enterprise income tax at 20% on taxable income; deduction of the provisional tax paid in September, any withholding tax credit on interest/dividends/fees, and the current-year tax payable or refundable amount.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Tax withheld at source on any interest paid to overseas lenders and royalties to the parent may be credited only when evidenced by withholding tax certificates; the final tax payable amount is the base for quarterly instalment calculations for the following year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Retained Earnings Surcharge Worksheet (Unappropriated Earnings Schedule)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computation of the 5% surcharge on retained, undistributed earnings after legal reserve transfers, accrued dividends, and other statutory appropriations.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Decision between dividend distribution (21% non-resident WHT at source) versus retention (5% surcharge at entity level) must be modelled before filing; a Chinese parent unable to obtain treaty relief should assess the China foreign tax credit position when electing the distribution route.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: penalty of 3% of the assessed tax and any deficiency for each month or part of a month in arrears, capped at 30% (Income Tax Act Article 108). Late payment: 1% surcharge for every two days of delay, capped at 15%, plus interest on the unpaid balance (Article 112). Failure to file withholding statements or to remit withheld tax attracts fines up to NT$15,000 per statement and an additional surcharge of up to 20% of the unremitted withholding amount.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 21% final withholding tax on dividends distributed to non-resident shareholders out of profits earned in fiscal years beginning on or after 1 January 2018 (20% statutory rate applies to prior-year profit pools); the Taiwan paying entity must withhold at source and file the withholding return within ten days of payment.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke a Taiwan income-tax agreement, the beneficial owner must submit Form 105 (Application for Application of Tax Agreement) to the withholding agent or the local tax authority before or at the date of the dividend distribution. Submission requires: (1) a Certificate of Residence (COR/Living Certificate) issued by the beneficial owner's competent tax authority, (2) documentary proof of beneficial ownership, (3) a shareholders' register and board resolution of the Taiwan entity, and (4) for a PRC-resident shareholder, a Chinese business tax number certificate. Taiwan's DTA network generally reduces dividend withholding to 10% or 5% for substantial holdings. Critical cross-strait note: the Cross-Strait Comprehensive Economic Cooperation Agreement tax arrangement has been signed but is not in force; the Chinese parent cannot claim the 5% DTA rate and remains subject to the full 21% statutory WHT. The Chinese parent can, however, claim a foreign tax credit in China under Enterprise Income Tax Law Article 23, crediting the 21% Taiwan WHT against its 25% Chinese corporate income tax, subject to direct-credit limitations and the five-year carryforward of excess credits.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory withholding rates for payments by the Taiwan entity to non-resident recipients: royalties for use of patents, trademarks, and know-how - 20%; interest on intercompany loans, foreign bonds, and ordinary debt - 20%. Treaty rates are frequently reduced to 10% for royalties and 10% for interest under Taiwan's bilateral agreements with major jurisdictions; no reduction is available for payments to a PRC parent because no cross-strait DTA is in force. The Taiwan payer must file the withholding return and pay the withheld tax to the Treasury within ten days of each payment, and interest paid to related foreign parties is disallowed as a deduction where the debtor has excessive thin-capitalisation (fixed at a debt-to-equity ratio of 3:1).

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Transfer pricing documentation (Local File equivalent) is statutorily required for a Taiwan resident enterprise when, in a fiscal year, related-party transactions with a single related party exceed NT$20 million, or aggregate related-party transactions exceed NT$50 million (New Taiwan Dollars). Master File documentation is required only where the Taiwan enterprise is the ultimate parent or surrogate parent of a multinational group filing Country-by-Country reports; CbC reporting applies where the consolidated group revenue exceeds approximately NT$27 billion. Low-risk routine bunker-distribution functions may be exempted from preparing the full report if the taxpayer functions as a limited-risk distributor or terminal operator and satisfies the criteria of the Transfer Pricing Examination Guidelines.
approved_arm_length_methodologies: Comparable Uncontrolled Price (CUP) method - suitable for benchmarked bunker fuel sales against public Singapore Platts pricing and exchange-quoted jet-fuel indices
Resale price method - applicable for the Taiwan entity buying from related-party traders and reselling to independent vessel operators
Cost plus method - appropriate for tolling, logistics, and lubricant-blending services performed for the parent
Transactional Net Margin Method (TNMM) - standard approach where the Taiwan entity is a routine distributor earning a terminal-operator margin
Profit split method - required when each side contributes unique intangibles or assumes significant distribution risks in joint fuel procurement ventures
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Taiwan does not maintain a stand-alone regulatory scheme called 'Economic Substance Regulations', but the Substantive Taxation Principle under the Taxpayer Rights Protection Act and the general anti-avoidance rules in the Income Tax Act and the Basic Income Tax Regime allow the tax authority to recharacterise artificial arrangements. Since tax year 2023, Taiwan's CFC rules and effective-management-place doctrine impose a substance requirement on foreign-incorporated entities controlled by Taiwan residents; a Taiwan filing entity performing marine bunkering must demonstrate permanent local substance: licensed storage and barge-custody arrangements, locally resident trading and operations staff, independent board decisions, a substantive bank account receiving invoiced proceeds, and real risk management over credit, fuel-price, and vessel-delivery risks. Absent such substance, the tax authority may reallocate the bunkering profit to the Chinese parent and disregard the Taiwan entity as a conduit.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately under-reporting USD-denominated bunker sales to shell shipowners, issuing false or suppressed invoices for bonded fuel deliveries at international anchorage areas, redirecting sale proceeds to personal or Hong Kong/UAE bank accounts, or failing to declare gross revenue from bunker sales delivered within Taiwan's territorial waters.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Deficiency assessment including the 20% income tax and the 5% retained earnings surtax; late-payment surcharge of 1% per two days (up to 15%); a fine of up to twice the evaded tax under Article 110 of the Income Tax Act; criminal prosecution for intentional evasion carries imprisonment of not more than two years and/or a fine of up to NT$150,000.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The responsible director, CFO, or de facto manager who signed or caused the false filing is personally subject to criminal imprisonment; the tax authority may seize the director's personal assets and impose a restriction on leaving Taiwan (travel ban) where the entity's overdue tax exceeds the statutory threshold under the Tax Collection Act; civil restitution for damage to the corporate estate can be pursued under Article 23 of the Company Act.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Sham Structure and Shell Company Abuse
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operationalising a paper Taiwan company with no employees, no fuel-supply licence, no tank or barge custody, no physical office, and no bank account, used exclusively to re-invoice bunker transactions between the Chinese parent and third-country shipowners in order to strip profit from China and characterise it as Taiwan-source trading income.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Recharacterisation under the substantive taxation principle; the tax authority will deny the Taiwan entity's income attribution and reallocate the entire margin to the Chinese parent under Article 43-1 (related-party reallocation); the Taiwan entity is assessed at 20% on deemed constructive profits plus 5% surtax on deemed undistributed earnings, followed by a transfer-pricing penalty and a fine of up to twice the underpaid tax; issuance of fabricated VAT invoices exposes the entity to suspension and criminal prosecution.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Nominee directors who sign false board minutes, contracts, and invoices face personal criminal liability under the Commercial Accounting Act for falsifying invoices (imprisonment up to five years); the corporate veil may be pierced where the company is used to defraud the tax authority, exposing the beneficial Chinese owner to joint personal and civil liability; responsible persons are also subject to travel bans and asset freezes during the tax investigation.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Processing SWIFT wire or standby LC payments for vessels listed on OFAC, EU, or UN sanctions lists; failing to perform customer due diligence and to file a Suspicious Transaction Report where a customer makes cash prepayments exceeding the NT$500,000 threshold, uses layered offshore shell ownership, or requests unusual rerouting of bunker payments through third-country jurisdictions without economic justification.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Money Laundering Control Act, failure to perform CDD or to file an STR is punishable by a fine of NT$500,000 to NT$10,000,000; wilful facilitation of money laundering through the bunker-supply payment chain carries imprisonment of up to two years; the company may be barred from operating the bunkering licence and have its vessels and bunker storage subject to judicial seizure.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: AML compliance officers, the responsible director, and the CFO who knowingly approve sanctioned-vessel payments or conceals STR obligation are individually liable with fines and imprisonment; personal travel restrictions and asset freezes are applied by the prosecutor; a criminal conviction additionally carries disqualification from serving as a director for up to three years and potential civil liability for creditor losses.
